title: Dermatologist visit
what: A doctor who treats conditions of the skin, hair, and nails, and checks moles.
why: For rashes, itching, acne, spots, hair loss, nail fungus, or changing moles.
tell_doctor: When it appeared and how it has changed
What you have already applied or taken

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: On the day of the visit, do not put cream or ointment on the area. The doctor needs to see it as it is.

prepare.title: Makeup
prepare.text: If it is your face, come without makeup. If it is your nails, no nail polish.

prepare.title: Photos
prepare.text: If the rash comes and goes, take photos of it.

bring: Photos of the rash, if you have them
Names of creams and ointments you used
Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
Your skin is checked in good light
Moles are looked at through a special magnifier called a dermatoscope
Sometimes a skin scraping is taken for testing
feel: A scraping feels like a light scratch, almost painless
after: Apply treatments as the doctor said, and do not stop the course early
red_flags: Fast-growing swelling of the face or lips, or a rash with a high fever: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I put cream on the rash before the visit?
faq.a: Best not on the day of the visit. The doctor needs to see the skin without ointment.

faq.q: How often should moles be checked?
faq.a: Usually once a year, unless your doctor says otherwise. More often if a mole changes.

reminders.text: Dermatologist visit tomorrow. No cream on the area, and come without makeup or nail polish.
